chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ghiyath ibn Ibrahim, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), that the Commander of the Believers (peace be upon him) said:
Do not slaughter the sheep in the presence of another sheep, nor the camel in the presence of another camel, while it is looking at it.

key_terms.الشَّاةَ: sheep or small livestock (goat, ewe); used here for small slaughter animals
key_terms.الْجَزُورَ: camel designated for slaughter; specifically a large slaughter animal
key_terms.يَنْظُرُ إِلَيْهِ: is looking at it; the live animal witnessing the slaughter

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible in Islam to slaughter an animal in front of another animal of the same species?
ai.summary: This hadith transmits a ruling from Imam Ali (peace be upon him), reported through Imam al-Sadiq, prohibiting the slaughter of an animal in the sight of another animal of the same species. The ruling reflects an Islamic ethic of merciful treatment toward animals, recognizing that witnessing slaughter causes distress to the observing animal. This principle was well-understood in the early Islamic community where animal husbandry was common, and the prohibition emphasizes that care for animals extends even to the manner of slaughter.

en.hubeali:
Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Gayas Bin Ibrahim, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> that Amir Al-Momineen<sup>asws</sup> said:
‘Do not slaughter the sheep in the presence of the sheep, nor a camel in the presence of the camel, and it is looking at it’.
en.sarwar: 7. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Muhammad ibn Yahya from Ghiyath ibn Ibrahim who has said the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said that ’Amir al-Mu’minin has said, ‘
Do not slaughter a sheep near another sheep or a camel near another camel when it is looking to the one being slaughtered.’ ”
